irregularities.item: KXXBANNEDGROK and KXXBANNEDMURRAYHILLGUY1 list non-official settlement sources (google.com search URLs, a blank-name placeholder 'account holder of ', and an individual's X profile).
KXBRYSONCOURSERECORDS uses an individual's YouTube channel as its settlement source.
PRESPARTYOH names 'Library of Congress' but links to congress.gov. KXZAMBIAPRES links to generic kalshi.com instead of the named electoral authority.
POPVOTEDJTFL is titled 'Trump Florida' and lists United States Congress as its only source.

For the three settled KXAAAGASW markets on 2026-11-16, settlement_ts (13:58:49Z) is earlier than expected_expiration_time (15:00:00Z). The rule refers to 'Nov 16, 2026' per AAA. Confirm how the settlement timestamp relates to the AAA daily average.
Market titles in the gas series contain markdown markup ('**gas prices**').
Kalshi documents that demo market prices and behaviour may not reflect real markets. Demo and production credentials are not interchangeable.
Kalshi documents that GET /markets/{ticker} is cached briefly, so prices and status can lag by a few seconds. Live charts therefore cannot claim tick-level accuracy.
The Market object exposes volume in contracts (volume_fp) and a $1 notional value per contract, but no dollar-volume field. Ranking 'by dollar amount' requires a definition not provided by the API.
Repository root contains only README.md ('# Demo3'). No license, .gitignore, or COORDINATION.md existed on main at base commit 80f7c4d.

questions.q: What does 'highest dollar amount' mean for ranking?
questions.known: The Market object provides volume_fp (contracts traded), open_interest_fp (contracts), and notional_value_dollars ($1.00 per contract at settlement). It provides no dollar-volume field.
questions.missing: A ranking definition. Options: contract volume, open interest, or an estimated notional computed from price.

questions.known: KXAAAGASW (US gas price up, AAA source) is in the Economics category.
questions.missing: Other gas-price series or events. The category filter for 'Energy and Commodities' returned no series.

questions.q: Can the browser reach the Kalshi public API?
questions.known: The public API is documented as needing no authentication for market data.
questions.missing: Whether browsers on GitHub Pages are allowed by CORS. This could not be tested from the build sandbox.

questions.q: Are seconds-level price charts possible from REST alone?
questions.known: Candlestick periods are 1 minute, 60 minutes, or 1 day. The most recent candles can be a few seconds behind trades.
questions.missing: A decision on whether to add WebSocket streaming for true sub-minute data.

questions.q: Which environment should the portfolio analysis use?
questions.known: Demo and production keys are separate. Demo prices may not reflect real markets.
questions.missing: A decision on whether analysis uses demo data, production data, or both.

questions.q: What are the actual fees for planned trades?
questions.known: Series expose fee_type (for example quadratic) and fee_multiplier.
questions.missing: Fee amounts from the fee schedule (not parsed).

questions.q: What is the public rate limit?
questions.known: Unauthenticated requests have separate limits. Authenticated requests are token-based, with 429 responses when exceeded.

questions.q: How are markets resolved and paid?
questions.known: Each contract pays $1 to the correct side. Results are yes, no, or scalar. Settlement runs after a timer (settlement_timer_seconds).
questions.missing: Confirmation that every settlement source is an official, stable source (see irregularities I-01 to I-04).

questions.q: Do settled gas markets resolve before the expected expiration?
questions.known: Three settled KXAAAGASW markets have settlement_ts before expected_expiration_time.
questions.missing: An explanation from Kalshi or a check of AAA methodology (see I-05).

questions.q: Are there API credentials for the demo account?
questions.known: Authenticated endpoints require an API key ID and an RSA-PSS or Ed25519 signature.
questions.missing: A demo API key. Creating one requires the account owner to log in to demo.kalshi.co.

questions.q: What trading strategy objectives and risk limits apply?
questions.known: None stated in the project request beyond tracking, analysis, and categorisation.
questions.missing: Position sizing, maximum loss, categories to trade, and stop rules.

questions.q: How long should the live window run for each market?
questions.known: Markets move through initialized, active, closed, determined, and finalized statuses.
questions.missing: A rule for when tracking stops. The dashboard keeps tracked markets until they finalize.

suggestions.title: Stream prices over WebSocket for seconds-level charts
suggestions.detail: REST candlesticks cannot show seconds. A WebSocket subscription can provide live price and orderbook updates.
options: A. Keep REST polling in the browser (current)
B. Add a WebSocket feed in the browser (needs CORS test)
C. Add a small server-side relay (needs hosting)

suggestions.title: Define the dollar ranking
suggestions.detail: The API has no dollar-volume field. Pick a definition before ranking by dollars.
options: C. Rank by estimated notional (contracts x price, labelled as an estimate)

suggestions.title: Schedule snapshot refreshes
suggestions.detail: A scheduled GitHub Action could save verified snapshots each hour, so the static pages keep history even when browsers cannot reach the API.

suggestions.title: Score settlement sources before trading
suggestions.detail: Tag each market as official, non-official, or unclear, and exclude unclear markets from strategy tests.
options: B. Exclude flagged markets from analysis
C. Exclude and require manual review

suggestions.title: Read-only portfolio before any trading
suggestions.detail: Connect the demo account read-only first (balance, positions, fills), then add trading only after analysis is trusted.

suggestions.title: Paper-test strategies before executing
suggestions.detail: Replay historical candlesticks to test each trade category before any order is placed.
options: A. Backtest on historical candles first
B. Trade small on demo first

suggestions.title: Keep demo and production data separate
suggestions.detail: Label every table with its environment. Use demo only for execution tests and production data for market analysis.

findings.text: Three settled KXAAAGASW markets for 2026-11-16 all resolved YES. Each strike was below the recorded expiration value of 3.8118.
Settled gas markets report settlement_value_dollars of 1.0000, which matches Kalshi's documented $1 per winning contract.
Culture and some golf and elections series use settlement sources that are not official (see Flagged for Review). These are the highest-risk categories for resolution disputes.
Portfolio and trade analysis cannot be produced yet. Authenticated endpoints need a demo API key that does not exist in this workspace.
